It was founded by Chicago broadcaster Bruce DuMont, who began building the museum in 1982; the museum's own press material gives its founding year as 1983, a one-year discrepancy this record shows rather than resolves. The museum first opened in a physical location in June 1987 in the River City condominium complex at 800 S. Wells Street, moved to the Chicago Cultural Center in 1992, and later built its own building at 360 N. State Street, which opened in 2012. Since 1991 the MBC has been the home of the National Radio Hall of Fame: that year DuMont assumed control of the Hall, moved its base of operations to Chicago, and incorporated it into the museum, where its gallery has been housed. DuMont retired from the museum in 2017; he died in September 2025, and the museum's leadership has since overseen planning for its next location while the Radio Hall of Fame inductions continue in Chicago.

name: Jalen Hurts
description: Jalen Alexander Hurts (born August 7, 1998, in Houston, Texas) is an American professional football quarterback for the Philadelphia Eagles of the National Football League. A coach's son, he was coached by his father Averion at Channelview High School in Texas, then played college football at Alabama from 2016 to 2018, where he was part of the 2017 national championship team, before finishing his college career at Oklahoma in 2019. Philadelphia drafted him in the second round of the 2020 NFL draft, 53rd overall, and he became the Eagles' starter late in his rookie season. In the 2022 season he led Philadelphia to Super Bowl LVII — the first Super Bowl to feature two Black starting quarterbacks, Hurts and Patrick Mahomes — and earned second-team All-Pro and Pro Bowl honors while finishing second in AP NFL Most Valuable Player voting. On February 9, 2025, he led the Eagles to a 40–22 victory over Kansas City in Super Bowl LIX and was voted the game's Most Valuable Player. Hurts remains Philadelphia's starting quarterback in the 2026 season, among the defining Black quarterbacks of his generation.

name: Kevin Hart
description: Kevin Darnell Hart (born July 6, 1979, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) is an American comedian and actor, raised in Philadelphia by his mother Nancy, who worked as a systems analyst at the University of Pennsylvania. After amateur comedy competitions around New England and a recurring role on the television series Undeclared, he built his reputation through stand-up releases beginning with I'm a Grown Little Man in 2008 and film roles including Think Like a Man (2012), Ride Along (2014), and Central Intelligence (2016). His What Now? tour made him, by Forbes's accounting for June 2015 to June 2016, the highest-paid comedian in the world, ending Jerry Seinfeld's decade at the top of Forbes's list. Time magazine named him to the Time 100, its list of the 100 most influential people in the world, in 2015, and in 2017 he launched the Laugh Out Loud Network in partnership with Lionsgate. Hart remains an active touring comedian and film star in 2026, one of the most commercially successful stand-up performers of his era.

name: Marvel Cooke
description: Marvel Jackson Cooke (April 1903 – November 2000) was a pioneering Black American journalist whose career ran from the Harlem Renaissance press to a mainstream metropolitan daily. Born in Mankato, Minnesota, and educated at the University of Minnesota, she came to New York as an editorial assistant at The Crisis in 1925 and joined the New York Amsterdam News in 1928, where the Schomburg Center's guide to her oral history records her as the paper's first female news reporter. With Ella Baker she wrote “The Bronx Slave Market” for The Crisis in 1935, exposing the street-corner markets where Black domestic workers were hired by the day at exploitative wages. From 1942 to 1947 she was assistant managing editor of The People's Voice. In 1950 the New York Daily Compass hired her, making her the first African American woman to work as a reporter for a mainstream, white-owned American daily newspaper, and she returned to the slave markets undercover for a five-part series, “The Bronx Slave Market,” in January 1950 that drew official responses on behalf of domestic workers. Cooke died in New York in November 2000, a few months short of her one hundredth birthday.

name: Romeo Santos
aliases: Anthony Santos; Anthony "Romeo" Santos; The King of Bachata
description: Romeo Santos, born Anthony Santos on 21 July 1981 in the Bronx, New York City, is a Dominican-American singer, songwriter and producer known as the King of Bachata. Born to a Dominican father and a Puerto Rican mother, he sang in a church choir as a child and co-founded the bachata group Aventura in the Bronx, serving as its lead vocalist, frontman and principal songwriter. Aventura fused bachata with R&B, hip-hop and pop, breaking through internationally with “Obsesión,” which spent sixteen weeks at No. 1 in Italy. After Aventura split in 2011, Santos launched a solo career with Fórmula, Vol. 1 (2011), followed by Fórmula, Vol. 2 (2014), carrying “Propuesta Indecente” and “Odio,” featuring Drake, and sold-out stadium shows including Yankee Stadium. Golden (2017), Utopía (2019) and Fórmula, Vol. 3 (2022) completed his solo run through the trilogy. In November 2025 he released Better Late Than Never, a collaborative album with Prince Royce that debuted at No. 1 on Billboard's Top Tropical Albums, and in 2026 he co-headlined the Mejor Tarde Que Nunca tour across the United States, Europe and Latin America.

name: Désiré Doué
description: Désiré Doué, born on 3 June 2005 in Angers, France, is a French winger of Ivorian descent who plays for Paris Saint-Germain and the France national team. He joined Rennes as a child and made his senior debut in August 2022, becoming the first player born in 2005 to score in one of Europe's top five leagues. Paris Saint-Germain signed him in August 2024 on a five-year contract. He made his senior France debut in March 2025, and on 31 May 2025 he produced the defining performance of the Champions League final in Munich: two goals and an assist in PSG's 5–0 win over Inter Milan, the club's first European Cup, earning player of the match as the first teenager to score twice in a Champions League final. He was named the UEFA Champions League Young Player of the Season and won the 2025 Golden Boy award.

name: Julián Quiñones
description: Julián Quiñones, born Julián Andrés Quiñones Quiñones on 24 March 1997 in Magüí Payán, Nariño, Colombia, is an Afro-Colombian professional footballer who plays as a forward for Al-Qadsiah of the Saudi Pro League and, by naturalization, for the Mexico national team. Raised in Colombia's Pacific-coast Afro-Colombian heartland, he entered Tigres UANL's youth system in 2015 and built his name at Atlas, winning back-to-back Liga MX titles (Apertura 2021 and Clausura 2022), before a permanent Atlas move, a 2023 transfer to Club América that brought two further league titles, and a June 2024 move to Al-Qadsiah reported at the time as the most expensive sale by a Mexican club. Naturalized as a Mexican citizen in October 2023, he won the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup with Mexico and scored the opening goal of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, against South Africa on 11 June 2026. He finished the 2025–26 Saudi season as the league's Golden Boot winner.

name: Marcus Rashford
description: Marcus Rashford, born on 31 October 1997 in Wythenshawe, Manchester, England, is an English forward for Manchester United and the England national team. A United academy product from the age of seven, he scored twice on his first-team debut against Midtjylland in February 2016 and twice more on his Premier League debut against Arsenal three days later, then scored on his England debut that May, becoming the youngest English player to score in his first senior international match. With United he has won the Europa League, FA Cups and EFL Cups. Off the pitch, his 2020 campaign on child food poverty — drawing on his own childhood experience of food insecurity — persuaded the UK government to extend free school meal vouchers over the summer holidays, and he was appointed MBE in the 2020 Birthday Honours. After a loan at Aston Villa in 2025, he spent 2025–26 on loan at Barcelona, winning La Liga, and returned to Manchester United in summer 2026 after Barcelona declined its purchase option.

name: Kobe Bryant
description: Kobe Bryant, born Kobe Bean Bryant on 23 August 1978 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was an American shooting guard who spent his entire 20-year NBA career with the Los Angeles Lakers. The son of NBA player Joe Bryant, he spent part of his childhood in Italy, starred at Lower Merion High School, and went straight to the NBA, chosen by the Charlotte Hornets with the 13th pick of the 1996 draft and traded to the Lakers. With Shaquille O'Neal he won three consecutive championships (2000–02), and he added two more as the team's leader in 2009 and 2010, winning Finals MVP both years; he was league MVP in 2008, an 18-time All-Star, and scored 81 points in a single game in 2006. He retired in 2016 with 33,643 career points and was voted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility. Bryant died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California, on 26 January 2020, aged 41, alongside his daughter Gianna and seven others.

name: Shaquille O'Neal
description: Shaquille O'Neal, born Shaquille Rashaun O'Neal on 6 March 1972 in Newark, New Jersey, is an American former professional basketball player and sports analyst, the dominant center of his era. After playing at Louisiana State University, he was selected first overall by the Orlando Magic in the 1992 NBA draft and named Rookie of the Year in 1993, leading Orlando to the 1995 NBA Finals. He signed with the Los Angeles Lakers in 1996 and, alongside Kobe Bryant, won three consecutive championships in 2000, 2001 and 2002, earning Finals Most Valuable Player honors each time and the league MVP award in 2000. Traded to the Miami Heat in 2004, he won a fourth championship in 2006. He closed his 19-year career with shorter stints in Phoenix, Cleveland and Boston, retiring in 2011 with 28,596 points and 15 All-Star selections. He was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016 and remains an analyst on Inside the NBA.

name: Bronny James
aliases: LeBron James Jr.; LeBron Raymone James Jr.
description: Bronny James, born LeBron James Jr. in 2004, is an American professional basketball player for the Los Angeles Lakers and the eldest son of LeBron James. A McDonald's All-American at Sierra Canyon School, he played one season at the University of Southern California, a freshman year delayed after he suffered cardiac arrest during a summer 2023 workout and underwent a procedure for a congenital heart defect; he averaged 4.8 points in 25 games. The Lakers selected him 55th overall in the 2024 NBA draft, and that October he and his father became the first father-son pair to play together in an NBA game. He has developed across his first two seasons between the Lakers and their G League program. In July 2026 his father left Los Angeles for Philadelphia, leaving Bronny as the lone James on the Lakers roster; entering his third season in October 2026, his salary for 2026-27 is fully guaranteed and Los Angeles continues to develop him as a rotation guard.

name: Victor Wembanyama
description: Victor Wembanyama, born 4 January 2004 in Le Chesnay, France, is a French professional basketball player for the San Antonio Spurs. The son of Felix Wembanyama, a track and field athlete of Congolese descent, and Elodie de Fautereau, a former basketball player and coach, he developed in France with Nanterre 92, ASVEL and Metropolitans 92, winning the French league's Most Valuable Player award in 2023. San Antonio selected him first overall in the 2023 NBA draft. He was the unanimous NBA Rookie of the Year in 2024, the first rookie named to the All-Defensive First Team, and he led France to a silver medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics. After a blood-clot diagnosis shortened his second season, he returned in 2025-26 to average career highs of 25.0 points and 11.5 rebounds, win Defensive Player of the Year as its youngest and first unanimous recipient, and carry San Antonio to the 2026 NBA Finals, where the Spurs fell to New York in five games. He signed a multi-year extension with San Antonio in July 2026.

name: Kevin Durant
aliases: Kevin Wayne Durant; KD; the Slim Reaper
description: Kevin Durant, born Kevin Wayne Durant on 29 September 1988 in Washington, D.C., is an American professional basketball player for the Houston Rockets. After one season at the University of Texas, where he was the first freshman named Naismith College Player of the Year, he was drafted second overall in 2007 by Seattle and won Rookie of the Year. With the franchise that became the Oklahoma City Thunder he won the league Most Valuable Player award in 2014 and four scoring titles. He joined Golden State in 2016 and won consecutive championships and Finals MVP awards in 2017 and 2018. After an Achilles injury in the 2019 Finals he played for Brooklyn and then Phoenix, passing 30,000 career points with the Suns. In July 2025 Phoenix traded him to Houston in the first seven-team trade in NBA history. In his first Houston season he averaged 26.0 points, and he entered a second Rockets season in October 2026 as the veteran centerpiece of a young roster.

name: Ja Morant
description: Ja Morant, born Temetrius Jamel Morant on 10 August 1999 in Dalzell, South Carolina, is an American professional basketball player for the Portland Trail Blazers. Lightly recruited out of Crestwood High School, he starred at Murray State, where as a sophomore he became the first player since assists became an official statistic to average 20 points and 10 assists in a season, won the Bob Cousy Award and was a consensus first-team All-American. Memphis drafted him second overall in 2019; he was Rookie of the Year in 2020, Most Improved Player and an All-NBA selection in 2022, and a two-time All-Star who led the Grizzlies to consecutive No. 2 seeds. Injuries and league suspensions — eight games in March 2023 and 25 games to open 2023-24, both over firearm incidents on social media — limited him to 79 games across his final three Memphis seasons. On 29 June 2026 Memphis traded him to Portland for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray, ending a seven-season tenure in which he averaged 22.4 points and 7.4 assists.

name: Kyrie Irving
description: Kyrie Irving, born Kyrie Andrew Irving on 23 March 1992 in Melbourne, Australia, to American parents and raised in West Orange, New Jersey, is an American professional basketball player for the Dallas Mavericks. After one season at Duke, Cleveland selected him first overall in the 2011 NBA draft and he was named Rookie of the Year. A nine-time All-Star, he won the 2014 All-Star Game MVP award and, in Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals, hit the decisive three-pointer that completed Cleveland's comeback against Golden State and delivered the Cavaliers' first championship. He later played for Boston and Brooklyn before a 2023 trade to Dallas, reaching a fourth Finals in 2024. He also won gold with the United States at the 2014 FIBA World Cup, where he was MVP, and at the 2016 Olympics. On 3 March 2025 he tore the ACL in his left knee and missed the whole 2025-26 season; in October 2026 he returned in preseason play in Macao, scoring 17 points against Houston.

name: Dylan Harper
description: Dylan Harper, born Dylan Robert Harper on 2 March 2006 in New Jersey, is an American professional basketball player for the San Antonio Spurs. He is the son of Ron Harper, the five-time NBA champion guard, and Maria Pizarro Harper, who emigrated from Bataan in the Philippines at age seven, played Division I basketball at the University of New Orleans and coached her son from childhood through high school. A McDonald's All-American at Don Bosco Prep, Harper played one season at Rutgers, averaging 19.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 4.0 assists and earning All-Big Ten honors. San Antonio selected him second overall in the 2025 NBA draft, making him one of the most prominent Filipino-descended players ever drafted. As a rookie he was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 2026 and emerged as a key rotation guard in San Antonio's run to the 2026 NBA Finals, including a 24-point, 11-rebound, seven-steal game against Oklahoma City in the conference finals.

name: Jayson Tatum
description: Jayson Tatum, born Jayson Christopher Tatum on 3 March 1998 in St. Louis, Missouri, is an American professional basketball player for the Boston Celtics. The Gatorade National Player of the Year at Chaminade College Preparatory School, he played one season at Duke before Boston selected him third overall in the 2017 NBA draft. A six-time All-Star and four-time All-NBA First Team selection, he was the Eastern Conference finals MVP in 2022 and led Boston to the 2024 NBA championship, the franchise's first title since 2008. He also won Olympic gold medals with the United States in Tokyo in 2021 and Paris in 2024. In May 2025 he ruptured his Achilles tendon; he returned in March 2026 and averaged 21.7 points across Boston's final regular-season games before knee stiffness held him out of the Celtics' final playoff game. By October 2026 he was healthy, leading a reworked Boston roster into his tenth season after the trade of Jaylen Brown.

name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
aliases: Giannis Sina Ugo Antetokounmpo; Giannis Sina Ugo Adetokunbo; Greek Freak
description: Giannis Antetokounmpo, born Giannis Sina Ugo Adetokunbo on 6 December 1994 in Athens, Greece, is a Greek-Nigerian professional basketball player for the Miami Heat. Born and raised in Athens to Nigerian parents, he played for Filathlitikos before Milwaukee selected him 15th overall in the 2013 NBA draft. Nicknamed the Greek Freak for his size, speed and ball-handling, he won Most Improved Player in 2017, consecutive league Most Valuable Player awards in 2019 and 2020, and Defensive Player of the Year in 2020 — only the third player to win MVP and Defensive Player of the Year in the same season. In 2021 he led Milwaukee to its first championship since 1971 and was unanimous Finals MVP; he left the Bucks as their all-time leader in points, rebounds, assists, blocks, games and minutes, with ten All-Star selections. In June 2026 Milwaukee traded him and Bobby Portis to Miami, and he began the 2026-27 season ranked among the league's top power forwards with the Heat.

name: Devin Booker
description: Devin Booker, born Devin Armani Booker on 30 October 1996 in Grand Rapids, Michigan, is an American professional basketball player for the Phoenix Suns. The son of Melvin Booker, a former professional guard who starred at Missouri, and Veronica Gutierrez, he moved to Moss Point, Mississippi, to live with his father in high school and became a McDonald's All-American. After one season at Kentucky, where he was the Southeastern Conference Sixth Man of the Year, Phoenix drafted him 13th overall in 2015. At 20 he scored a franchise-record 70 points against Boston, the youngest player ever to score more than 60 in a game. He led Phoenix to the 2021 NBA Finals and earned All-NBA First Team honors in 2022. A five-time All-Star and a two-time Olympic gold medalist, he became the Suns' all-time leading scorer in February 2025. In June 2026 he changed his jersey from No. 1 to No. 15, his father's Missouri number, for the 2026-27 season.

name: Lonzo Ball
description: Lonzo Ball, born Lonzo Anderson Ball on 27 October 1997 in Anaheim, California, is an American point guard whose career has been shaped by elite playmaking and a persistent left-knee injury. At Chino Hills High School he played alongside his brothers LiAngelo and LaMelo on a team that finished 35-0 in his senior season and took consensus national honors. In one season at UCLA he led the nation in assists, set the school single-season assists record, earned consensus first-team All-American honors and won the Wayman Tisdale Award. The Los Angeles Lakers selected him second overall in the 2017 NBA draft, and he made the NBA All-Rookie Second Team in 2018. Traded to New Orleans in 2019 in the Anthony Davis deal, he played two seasons for the Pelicans before joining the Chicago Bulls in a 2021 sign-and-trade. A meniscus tear in January 2022 and a cartilage transplant in March 2023 cost him the full 2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons; he returned for 35 games with Chicago in 2024-25, then played 35 games for Cleveland in 2025-26 before a February 2026 trade and waiver left him a free agent.

name: Tristan Thompson
description: Tristan Thompson, born Tristan Trevor James Thompson on 13 March 1991 in Brampton, Ontario, Canada, is a Canadian-American former center and one of the most successful Canadian players of his generation, raised by parents of Jamaican descent. After one season at the University of Texas, where he was Big 12 Freshman of the Year, Cleveland selected him fourth overall in the 2011 NBA draft — at the time the highest a Canadian had ever been picked. He made the NBA All-Rookie Second Team and became the Cavaliers' durable interior anchor, twice leading the league in games played. Starting all 21 playoff games, he helped Cleveland win the 2016 NBA championship, the first in franchise history, coming back from a 3-1 Finals deficit against Golden State. He later played for Boston, Sacramento, Indiana, Chicago and the Los Angeles Lakers before returning to Cleveland for 2023-25. Across 819 regular-season games he averaged 8.3 points and 7.8 rebounds. Unsigned through 2025-26, he confirmed his retirement as a player in 2026 and took a global ambassador role with Dubai Basketball.

name: Wilt Chamberlain
aliases: Wilton Norman Chamberlain; Wilt the Stilt; The Big Dipper
description: Wilt Chamberlain, born Wilton Norman Chamberlain on 21 August 1936 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was an American center whose records still define basketball's outer limits. A star at Philadelphia's Overbrook High School and at the University of Kansas, where he reached the 1957 NCAA final, he spent a season with the Harlem Globetrotters before joining the Philadelphia Warriors in 1959 and winning both Rookie of the Year and Most Valuable Player in his first season. On 2 March 1962 he scored 100 points in a single game, a record that still stands, and that season he averaged 50.4 points per game. He is the only player to average at least 30 points and 20 rebounds over an entire career, finishing with 31,419 points and an NBA-record 23,924 rebounds. Traded to the Philadelphia 76ers, he won his first championship in 1967, then moved to the Los Angeles Lakers in 1968, won a second title in 1972 and earned Finals MVP. A four-time league MVP and 13-time All-Star, he was enshrined in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1978. He died on 12 October 1999 in Los Angeles, California, at age 63.

name: Lamar Odom
description: Lamar Odom, born Lamar Joseph Odom on 6 November 1979 in Jamaica, Queens, New York, is an American former forward whose versatility made him a cornerstone of a championship team. Parade's national high school player of the year in 1997, he played one season at the University of Rhode Island before the Los Angeles Clippers selected him fourth overall in the 1999 NBA draft; he made the NBA All-Rookie First Team. After four seasons with the Clippers and one with the Miami Heat, he was traded to the Los Angeles Lakers in 2004 and spent seven seasons there, winning back-to-back championships in 2009 and 2010 and the NBA Sixth Man of the Year award in 2011. He later played for Dallas and again for the Clippers, and briefly in Spain in 2014, closing a 14-season career with averages of 13.3 points, 8.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists in 961 games. With the United States national team he won Olympic bronze in 2004 and FIBA World Championship gold in 2010. In October 2015 he was found unconscious in Nevada and hospitalized in a coma; he recovered and has spoken publicly since about addiction and recovery, most recently in a 2026 Netflix documentary.

name: Tyrese Haliburton
description: Tyrese Haliburton, born Tyrese John Haliburton on 29 February 2000 in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, is an American point guard for the Indiana Pacers. The son of John Haliburton, a referee and former women's coach, and Brenda Haliburton, he starred at Oshkosh North High School and then at Iowa State, where he set the program's single-game assists record and made the All-Big 12 second team as a sophomore. Sacramento selected him 12th overall in the 2020 NBA draft, and in February 2022 Indiana acquired him in the trade centered on Domantas Sabonis. In Indiana he became a two-time All-Star (2023, as a reserve, and 2024, as a starter) and a two-time All-NBA Third Team selection, and in 2025 he led the Pacers to their first NBA Finals appearance in 25 years. He won Olympic gold with the United States at Paris 2024. In Game 7 of the 2025 Finals he tore his right Achilles tendon and missed the entire 2025-26 season. After sixteen months of rehabilitation he returned in the October 2026 preseason, scoring 24 points in 18 minutes at Oklahoma City on his second game back.

name: Dennis Rodman
description: Dennis Rodman, born Dennis Keith Rodman on 13 May 1961 in Trenton, New Jersey, and raised in Dallas, Texas, is an American former forward regarded by NBA.com as arguably the best rebounding forward in the game's history. After a late growth spurt he starred at Southeastern Oklahoma State and was drafted by Detroit in the second round in 1986. With the Pistons' 'Bad Boys' he won championships in 1989 and 1990 and consecutive Defensive Player of the Year awards in 1990 and 1991. After two seasons in San Antonio he joined the Chicago Bulls in 1995 and completed their second three-peat, winning titles in 1996, 1997 and 1998 alongside Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen. He led the NBA in rebounds per game for a record seven consecutive seasons, made seven All-Defensive First Teams, and finished with 11,954 rebounds at 13.1 per game across fourteen seasons that closed with brief Lakers and Mavericks stops. Detroit retired his No. 10 jersey in 2011, and he was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame the same year and named to the NBA 75th Anniversary Team in 2021.

name: Russell Westbrook
description: Russell Westbrook, born 12 November 1988 in Long Beach, California, and raised in the Los Angeles area, is an American former point guard who retired in August 2026 as the NBA's all-time leader in triple-doubles. After Leuzinger High School in Lawndale and two seasons at UCLA, reaching consecutive Final Fours, he was drafted fourth overall in 2008 by Seattle, just before the franchise became the Oklahoma City Thunder. In eleven seasons in Oklahoma City he won the 2016-17 Most Valuable Player award, averaging a triple-double that season — a feat he repeated three more times — and set the single-season record with 42 triple-doubles. A nine-time All-Star, two-time scoring champion and three-time assists leader, he later played for Houston, Washington, the Los Angeles Lakers, the Los Angeles Clippers and Denver before closing with Sacramento in 2025-26, averaging 15.2 points, 6.7 assists and 5.4 rebounds in 64 games. He won Olympic gold at London 2012, was named to the NBA 75th Anniversary Team, and founded the Why Not? Foundation in 2012 for underserved communities in Los Angeles and beyond. He finished with 209 career triple-doubles.

name: Kawhi Leonard
description: Kawhi Leonard, born Kawhi Anthony Leonard on 29 June 1991 in Los Angeles, California, is an American forward for the Toronto Raptors and one of the defining two-way players of his era. California's Mr. Basketball at Riverside's Martin Luther King High School, he played two seasons at San Diego State, where his No. 15 was later retired, and was drafted 15th overall in 2011 by Indiana, which traded him to San Antonio on draft night. With the Spurs he won the 2014 championship and Finals MVP and consecutive Defensive Player of the Year awards in 2015 and 2016. Traded to Toronto in 2018, he delivered the Raptors' first championship in 2019, winning a second Finals MVP, then signed with the Los Angeles Clippers, where he played from 2019 to 2026. A seven-time All-Star and member of the NBA 75th Anniversary Team, he was traded back to Toronto on 30 June 2026 and opened the 2026-27 preseason with the Raptors in October 2026. On 2 September 2026 the NBA announced the outcome of its salary-cap circumvention investigation into his Clippers tenure, fining Leonard $700,000 in restitution while imposing larger penalties on the club and its owner.

name: A'ja Wilson
description: A'ja Wilson, born A'ja Riyadh Wilson on 8 August 1996 in Hopkins, South Carolina, is an American center for the Las Vegas Aces and the most decorated player in WNBA history by MVP count. Raised in the Columbia area and a star at Heathwood Hall, she played at the University of South Carolina under Dawn Staley, leading the Gamecocks to their first NCAA championship in 2017 as the tournament's Most Outstanding Player and becoming the school's all-time leading scorer. Las Vegas drafted her first overall in 2018, and she won Rookie of the Year. She has won five WNBA Most Valuable Player awards — in 2020, 2022, 2024, 2025 and 2026 — the last making her the first player ever to win three straight, and no other player has won more than three. She led the Aces to championships in 2022, 2023 and 2025, winning Finals MVP in 2023 and 2025, and in 2026 averaged a league-leading 26.2 points with 9.4 rebounds and a league-leading 1.9 blocks across 41 games. With the United States she has won two Olympic gold medals and two World Cup gold medals.

name: Carter Bryant
description: Carter Bryant, born Carter Dayne Bryant on 26 November 2005 in Riverside, California, is an American forward for the San Antonio Spurs. He grew up in a bilingual, bicultural household: his father, D'Cean Bryant, is African American, played college basketball at Long Beach State and later coached him in high school, and his mother, Sabrina Torres, is Latina and works as a sign-language interpreter; both of his maternal grandparents are deaf, and his grandfather is in the USA Deaf Basketball Hall of Fame. Bryant has said in his own words that he tries to represent the Latino community, the deaf community, Riverside and the African-American community alike. A McDonald's All-American at Corona Centennial, he played one season at the University of Arizona, averaging 6.5 points and 4.1 rebounds, and San Antonio selected him 14th overall in the 2025 NBA draft. As a rookie he played a reserve role for the Spurs, competed in the 2026 Slam Dunk Contest and won the 2026 Rising Stars Challenge, and he was on San Antonio's roster through the October 2026 preseason. He is not related to Kobe Bryant; reporting on his family background states there is no family connection between them.

name: Jared McCain
description: Jared McCain, born Jared Dane McCain on 20 February 2004 in Sacramento, California, is an American shooting guard for the Oklahoma City Thunder. His father, Lance McCain, is African-American, and McCain — a consensus five-star recruit at Centennial High School in Corona, twice California's Gatorade Player of the Year and the state's Mr. Basketball in 2023 — has also acknowledged a partial Filipino heritage. At Duke he made the ACC All-Rookie team in his single season, and Philadelphia selected him 16th overall in the 2024 NBA draft. As a rookie he led all rookies in scoring at 15.3 points per game and was named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for October-November 2024 before a December 2024 injury ended his season on 13 December. After a limited role in Philadelphia in 2025-26, he was traded to Oklahoma City at the February 2026 deadline and averaged 10.4 points in 30 regular-season games for the Thunder, then 12.5 points across eleven games in the Lakers and Spurs playoff series, starting two Western Conference Finals games. He opened the 2026-27 preseason with Oklahoma City in October 2026, scoring 20 points against Indiana.

name: Allen Iverson
aliases: Allen Ezail Iverson; The Answer; AI
description: Allen Iverson, born Allen Ezail Iverson on 7 June 1975 in Hampton, Virginia, is an American former guard whose game and presence reshaped basketball culture. At Bethel High School he won Virginia state championships in both football and basketball and was the Associated Press high school player of the year in both sports. At Georgetown he set the school's career scoring-average record at 23.0 points per game and won Big East Defensive Player of the Year twice in two seasons. Philadelphia selected him first overall in the 1996 NBA draft, and he won Rookie of the Year, four scoring titles and, in 2001, the league's Most Valuable Player award, carrying the 76ers to the 2001 NBA Finals. Listed at six feet, he averaged 26.7 points over a fourteen-season career spanning Philadelphia, Denver, Detroit and Memphis, made eleven All-Star teams and won two All-Star Game MVP awards. Britannica notes his influence on hip-hop culture alongside his explosive play. He retired in 2013, was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, and was named to the NBA 75th Anniversary Team in 2021.

name: Jason Taylor
description: Jason Taylor, born Jason Paul Taylor on 1 September 1974 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, is a retired American football defensive end whose fifteen-season career was anchored by the Miami Dolphins. A lightly recruited player who starred at the University of Akron, where he set a school record with 21 career sacks, he was selected by Miami in the third round, 73rd overall, of the 1997 NFL Draft and became a starter as a rookie. He anchored Miami's defense for more than a decade, led the NFL with 18.5 sacks in 2002, and in 2006 was named NFL Defensive Player of the Year. After single seasons with Washington in 2008 and the New York Jets in 2010, each followed by a return to Miami, he retired after the 2011 season with 139.5 career sacks. He was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2017, in his first year of eligibility, and has coached at the University of Miami since 2022, serving as the Hurricanes' defensive ends and rush coach from 2023 into the 2026 season.

name: Justin Jefferson
description: Justin Jefferson, born Justin Jamal Jefferson on 16 June 1999 in St. Rose, Louisiana, is an American football wide receiver for the Minnesota Vikings. He played at Destrehan High School and at LSU, where he helped the Tigers win the College Football Playoff national championship for the 2019 season. Minnesota selected him 22nd overall in the 2020 NFL Draft, and he answered with 1,400 receiving yards as a rookie. He has exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in every season of his career, including seasons shortened by injury. His 2022 season set the standard: he led the NFL with 128 receptions and 1,809 receiving yards and was named the Associated Press NFL Offensive Player of the Year. Through the first five weeks of the 2026 season he remained Minnesota's No. 1 receiver, recording 19 receptions for 258 yards and three touchdowns across four games played, and his career totals stood at 598 receptions for 8,738 yards and 45 receiving touchdowns in 98 games, all with the Vikings.

name: Lamar Jackson
description: Lamar Jackson, born Lamar Demeatrice Jackson Jr. on 7 January 1997 in Pompano Beach, Florida, is an American football quarterback for the Baltimore Ravens and the defining dual-threat quarterback of his generation. At the University of Louisville he won the Heisman Trophy in 2016, becoming the youngest winner in the award's history at the time and the first Cardinal to claim it. Baltimore selected him with the final pick of the first round, 32nd overall, in the 2018 NFL Draft, and he became the starter during his rookie season. In 2019, his first full season as a starter, he led the NFL in touchdown passes, set the single-season rushing record for a quarterback, and was voted NFL Most Valuable Player unanimously. He won a second MVP award for the 2023 season, when he led Baltimore to the AFC Championship Game, and in 2024 he set career highs in passing and became the NFL's all-time leader in rushing yards by a quarterback. He remained Baltimore's starting quarterback in the 2026 season.

name: Odell Beckham Jr.
description: Odell Beckham Jr., born 5 November 1992 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, is an American football wide receiver whose one-handed touchdown catch against Dallas on 23 November 2014 became one of the most replayed plays in NFL history. He attended Isidore Newman School in New Orleans and played at LSU before the New York Giants selected him 12th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. Despite missing the first four games of his rookie season he caught 91 passes for 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns and was named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year; across five seasons in New York he totaled 390 receptions for 5,476 yards and 44 touchdowns. Traded to Cleveland in 2019, he later joined the Los Angeles Rams during the 2021 season, scored the opening touchdown of Super Bowl LVI, and tore his ACL in the same game as the Rams won the championship. After seasons with Baltimore in 2023 and Miami in 2024, a brief 2026 return to the Giants ended with his release on 29 September 2026, and the Minnesota Vikings then signed him to their practice squad.

name: Damar Hamlin
description: Damar Hamlin, born Damar Romeyelle Hamlin on 24 March 1998 in McKees Rocks, Pennsylvania, is an American football safety for the Buffalo Bills. He attended Pittsburgh Central Catholic High School and played at the University of Pittsburgh, earning second-team All-ACC honors in 2020, before Buffalo selected him in the sixth round, 212th overall, of the 2021 NFL Draft. After a season as a backup he became a starter in 2022. On 2 January 2023, during a Monday Night Football game at Cincinnati, he suffered a cardiac arrest after making a tackle; his heartbeat was restored on the field, he was hospitalized in critical condition, and he was released from hospital nine days later. The episode was later attributed to commotio cordis, a rare disruption of the heart's rhythm caused by a blow to the chest. Cleared to play in April 2023, he returned during the 2023 season, started throughout 2024, and became a national advocate for CPR training and AED access through his Chasing M's Foundation. Buffalo re-signed him on a one-year deal in March 2026 for the 2026 season.

name: Jeremiah Smith
description: Jeremiah Smith, born Jeremiah Javon Smith on 29 November 2005 in Miami Gardens, Florida, is an American college football wide receiver for the Ohio State Buckeyes. He attended Chaminade-Madonna Prep in Hollywood, Florida, and arrived at Ohio State as one of the most heralded recruits in the country. As a true freshman in 2024 he caught 76 passes for 1,315 yards and 15 touchdowns, breaking FBS freshman receiving records, and helped Ohio State win the College Football Playoff national championship. As a sophomore in 2025 he added 87 receptions for 1,243 yards and 12 touchdowns and was named a unanimous All-American. By October of his junior season in 2026 he had broken all three of Ohio State's major career receiving records — receptions, receiving yards, and touchdown receptions — passing marks held by Emeka Egbuka, Michael Jenkins, and Chris Olave, and his career totals stood at 211 receptions for 3,474 yards and 38 touchdowns. He remains an Ohio State junior in the 2026 season and is not yet eligible for the NFL Draft.

name: Saquon Barkley
description: Saquon Barkley, born 9 February 1997 in the Bronx, New York, is an American football running back for the Philadelphia Eagles. Raised in Pennsylvania, he starred at Penn State and was selected by the New York Giants with the second overall pick of the 2018 NFL Draft, winning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year. After six seasons in New York he signed with Philadelphia in March 2024 and produced one of the greatest seasons ever played by a running back: 2,005 rushing yards in the regular season, making him the ninth player in NFL history to pass 2,000, plus 499 more rushing yards in the postseason. The Eagles won Super Bowl LIX over Kansas City on 9 February 2025, his 28th birthday, and Barkley was named NFL Offensive Player of the Year. Philadelphia then signed him to a two-year, $41.2 million extension that made him the first running back in NFL history to average more than $20 million per year. He remained Philadelphia's starting running back in the 2026 season, with 8,538 career rushing yards through Week 4.

name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
description: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, born 14 February 2002 in Nacogdoches, Texas, is an American football wide receiver for the Seattle Seahawks. He is of Sierra Leonean descent through his father: his paternal grandparents came from Sierra Leone, and as a high-school player he added "Njigba" — his grandfather's original surname, set aside for "Smith" on immigrating to the United States in the 1970s — to his own name to honor him. Raised in Rockwall, Texas, he starred at Ohio State, where his 347 receiving yards against Utah in the Rose Bowl on 1 January 2022 set the bowl's record. Seattle selected him 20th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. In 2025 he led the NFL with 1,793 receiving yards on 119 receptions, was named NFL Offensive Player of the Year, and helped Seattle win Super Bowl LX over New England in February 2026. That spring the Seahawks signed him to a four-year, $168.6 million extension, reported as the richest contract ever given to a wide receiver. He remains Seattle's No. 1 receiver in the 2026 season.

name: CeeDee Lamb
description: CeeDee Lamb, born Cedarian DeLeon Lamb on 8 April 1999 in Opelousas, Louisiana, is an American football wide receiver for the Dallas Cowboys. His family relocated to the Houston area after Hurricane Katrina, and he starred at Foster High School in Richmond, Texas, before playing at the University of Oklahoma, where he was a consensus All-American in 2019. Dallas selected him 17th overall in the 2020 NFL Draft and gave him the franchise's storied No. 88 jersey. He has been selected to the Pro Bowl in five of his first six seasons. His peak year to date was 2023, when he led the NFL with 135 receptions and set a Cowboys franchise record with 1,749 receiving yards, earning first-team All-Pro honors. In August 2024 he signed a four-year, $136 million extension with Dallas. Early in the 2026 season he remained the Cowboys' No. 1 receiver, and on 4 October 2026 he caught 17 passes for 189 yards, including the game-winning touchdown, in a 34–30 win at Houston; through five games he had 39 receptions for 507 yards and four touchdowns.

name: Melvin Van Peebles
description: Melvin Van Peebles (born Melvin Peebles, August 21, 1932, Chicago; died September 21, 2021, New York City, aged 89) was the filmmaker, writer, composer, and actor whose independent feature Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song (1971) opened the blaxploitation era and proved a Black-directed film could be financed outside the studio system and profit on its own terms. Raised in Chicago and educated at Ohio Wesleyan, he served in the Air Force, lived in the Netherlands and France, and made The Story of a Three-Day Pass (1967) from his French novel La Permission, winning an award at the San Francisco International Film Festival. A studio feature, Watermelon Man (1970), followed for Columbia. For Sweet Sweetback he wrote, directed, scored, and starred, raising roughly $150,000 independently; the film grossed just over $15 million. He also wrote the Broadway musical Ain't Supposed to Die a Natural Death (1971).

name: East-West All-Star Game
aliases: East-West Classic; Negro Leagues East-West All-Star Game
description: The East-West All-Star Game was the Negro leagues' annual showcase, first played September 10, 1933, at Comiskey Park in Chicago, where the West defeated the East 11–7 before 19,568 fans. Players were chosen by fan balloting conducted through Black newspapers; in the first vote Oscar Charleston led all players with 43,793 ballots and Willie Foster drew 40,637. Bill Foster pitched a complete game for the win and Mule Suttles hit the game's first home run. The classic ran from 1933 to 1950 and became Black America's premier recurring sporting event: the 1939 edition drew a record 40,000 fans, and the 1947 game outdrew that year's Major League Baseball All-Star Game at Wrigley Field by 7,000. Historian Larry Lester has called it the biggest event in Black America, with the sole exception of a Joe Louis fight.

name: Warren Moon
description: Warren Moon (born November 18, 1956, Los Angeles) is the quarterback whose career exposed and then outlasted the NFL's refusal to draft Black quarterbacks. At the University of Washington he was named MVP of the 1978 Rose Bowl, yet no NFL team drafted him, so he began his professional career in Canada, leading the Edmonton Eskimos to five consecutive Grey Cup championships (1978–1982), a CFL record, and winning two Grey Cup MVP awards. He then played seventeen NFL seasons, principally for the Houston Oilers (1984–1993), with later stops in Minnesota, Seattle, and Kansas City before retiring in 2000. Moon was named to nine Pro Bowls, was the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year in 1990, and threw for 49,325 NFL passing yards. In 2006 he became the first Black quarterback, and the first undrafted quarterback, inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame; he remains the only player in both the Pro Football and Canadian Football Halls of Fame.

name: Michael Reese Hospital
description: Michael Reese Hospital, founded in 1881 at 2929 South Ellis Avenue in Chicago's Bronzeville, was for more than a century one of the city's major research and teaching hospitals and one of its great medical employers. Its campus grew to 48 acres on the near South Side. The hospital also carried a documented role in Black Chicago's professional formation: the University of Illinois Chicago's Mapping Care project records its place in training and employing Black nurses, including Frances Barge, who in 1973 became the first Black director of a nursing school there. The Reese campus held 1,008 beds in 1991. Decline ended in closure: patients were transferred to Mercy Hospital by the end of 2008, the campus was vacated in January 2009, and the hospital's official closure date was August 31, 2009. Demolition ran from October 2009 to 2013, leaving the Singer Pavilion as the sole surviving building; the site is now planned as Bronzeville Lakefront.

name: L. Alex Wilson
description: L. Alex Wilson (Lucious Alexander Wilson) was the editor and general manager of the Memphis Tri-State Defender and one of the Black press's defining correspondents of the civil rights era. He covered the Korean War for the Chicago Defender in 1950, led the Defender newspaper chain's coverage of the Emmett Till case in 1955, and hired Dorothy Butler Gilliam, who became a pioneering Black woman journalist. On September 23, 1957, covering the Little Rock Nine in Arkansas, Wilson was beaten by a white mob on camera — struck with a brick and choked — and refused to run, an image of press courage carried on national television. He later became editor of the Chicago Defender. The 1957 assault's injuries shadowed the rest of his life; he died in 1960 at 51, of Parkinson's disease that the sources tie to the beating's damage. His birth year is not independently sourced in the accounts read and is shown only as the arithmetic of his reported age at death.

name: Joe Louis
aliases: Joseph Louis Barrow; The Brown Bomber
description: Joe Louis (born Joseph Louis Barrow, May 13, 1914, LaFayette, Alabama; died April 12, 1981, Paradise, Nevada) was the world heavyweight boxing champion from 1937 to 1949 and the most consequential Black athlete of his century. Raised in Detroit, he won the 1934 national AAU light-heavyweight title and took the heavyweight crown from James J. Braddock on June 22, 1937, at Chicago's Comiskey Park, knocking Braddock out in the eighth round. Louis had lost to Germany's Max Schmeling in 1936; their rematch on June 22, 1938, before 70,043 at Yankee Stadium, ended in two minutes and four seconds of the first round and was read worldwide as democracy's answer to Nazi racial doctrine. Louis defended the title 25 times, a division record, and his reign made him a unifying national hero and the standard against which Black athletic greatness was measured for a generation.

name: James R. Grossman
description: James R. Grossman is the historian whose Land of Hope: Chicago, Black Southerners, and the Great Migration (1989) set the scholarly frame for Chicago's Great Migration history — the book is already in this graph at CTL-E-5850, and this record completes its authorship. Grossman earned his bachelor's degree at Cornell and his doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley, taught at the University of Chicago and UC San Diego, and served as vice president for research and education at the Newberry Library in Chicago. His second book, A Chance to Make Good: African Americans 1900–1929, appeared in 1997, and he was a project director and co-editor of the Encyclopedia of Chicago. From 2010 to 2025 he served as executive director of the American Historical Association. In 2025 the Society of American Historians awarded him its Tony Horwitz Prize, honoring his leadership of the historical profession.

name: A'Lelia Bundles
description: A'Lelia Bundles is the author and journalist who wrote the definitive biography of her great-great-grandmother, Madam C. J. Walker. Her On Her Own Ground: The Life and Times of Madam C. J. Walker (Scribner, 2001), the product of more than twenty years of research, was the first full-scale biography of the beauty-industry pioneer, and it was adapted as the 2020 Netflix limited series Self Made: Inspired by the Life of Madam C. J. Walker, starring Octavia Spencer. Bundles came to the biography from a career as a veteran television news journalist and producer, including work at ABC News, per her publisher biographies. Her second Walker-family biography, Joy Goddess: A'Lelia Walker and the Harlem Renaissance (Scribner, June 10, 2025), turns to Walker's daughter — the author's namesake — and the Harlem Renaissance world she bankrolled and embodied. Bundles maintains the Walker research archive and site at aleliabundles.com.

name: Willie Thrower
description: Willie Thrower (Willie Lee Thrower Sr., born March 22, 1930, New Kensington, Pennsylvania; died February 20, 2002) was the first Black quarterback to play in the modern National Football League. At Michigan State he was the first Black quarterback in the Big Ten and a member of the Spartans' 1952 national championship team. Signed by the Chicago Bears, Thrower made his NFL debut on October 18, 1953, against the San Francisco 49ers at Wrigley Field, relieving George Blanda and completing three of eight passes for 27 yards with one interception — the first appearance by a Black quarterback in the modern NFL, as the Bears' own history records it. The Bears released him after the 1953 season, and the league's color line at quarterback held for years more. Warren Moon thanked Thrower by name in his 2006 Pro Football Hall of Fame speech; a statue of Thrower was unveiled at his Valley High School in 2006.

name: Sengstacke Enterprises
description: Sengstacke Enterprises was the Black newspaper chain built by John H. Sengstacke around the Chicago Defender, which he took over in 1940 and from which he also founded the National Newspaper Publishers Association. From 1965 Sengstacke assembled the chain outward from Chicago: the Pittsburgh Courier was purchased and reopened as the New Pittsburgh Courier in 1967, and the Memphis Tri-State Defender and Detroit's Michigan Chronicle joined the Chicago Defender in the group. When Sengstacke died in May 1997, Sengstacke Enterprises held those four papers, and congressional tributes entered into the Record in 1997 and 2000 describe the chain as his life's structure. In 2000, Editor & Publisher reported, the board of Sengstacke Enterprises Inc. voted to auction the Defender and the three weeklies under the pressure of an estate-tax bill of roughly three million dollars. The Defender survives as the flagship of Real Times Media.

name: Gerri Oliver
description: Gerri Oliver — Geraldine “Mama Gerri” Oliver — was the proprietor who made Gerri's Palm Tavern at 446 East 47th Street the premier gathering place of Bronzeville for nearly half a century. A Mississippi native who had worked as a manicurist, she bought the tavern in 1956 from James “Genial Jim” Knight, who had opened it in 1933 and held court as the first “Mayor of Bronzeville.” Under Oliver the Palm Tavern hosted Duke Ellington, Dizzy Gillespie, Billie Holiday, James Brown, Lena Horne, Muddy Waters, and Quincy Jones, and Harold Washington celebrated his 1983 mayoral victory there. The city boarded the building up in an eminent-domain taking in August 2001, and it was later demolished; the tavern itself is homed in the graph at CTL-E-0145. Oliver died on December 7, 2020, at the age of 101, in California. She is a distinct person from Gerri Major, the journalist — the shared first name is a documented collision trap in the sources, and this record is built on the Palm Tavern proprietor only.

name: Bessie Smith
description: Bessie Smith, born in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and killed in a car crash near Clarksdale, Mississippi, on September 26, 1937, was the “Empress of the Blues” and the most commanding blues singer of the recording era's first decades. Orphaned young, she sang for pennies on Chattanooga street corners, joined Ma Rainey's orbit about 1912–1913, and signed with Columbia Records in February 1923. Her first coupling, including “Down Hearted Blues,” was a phenomenon, and across roughly 160 Columbia recordings between 1923 and the early 1930s she worked with Fletcher Henderson, Louis Armstrong — their 1925 “St. Louis Blues” is a canonical recording — Benny Goodman, and Coleman Hawkins. Smith headlined the Theater Owners Booking Association circuit and was, by wide agreement, the highest-paid Black entertainer of her time. She was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989.

name: E. Franklin Frazier
description: E. Franklin Frazier (Edward Franklin Frazier, born September 24, 1894, Baltimore; died May 17, 1962, Washington, D.C.) was the sociologist who defined the scholarly study of the Black family in America. He earned his bachelor's at Howard University in 1916, a master's at Clark in 1920, and his doctorate at the University of Chicago in 1931; the dissertation became The Negro Family in Chicago (1932), and its expansion, The Negro Family in the United States (1939), won the Anisfield-Wolf Award in 1940. He directed the Atlanta School of Social Work from 1922 to 1927, chaired Howard's sociology department, became the first Black president of the American Sociological Association in 1948, and helped draft UNESCO's 1950 statement The Race Question. His Black Bourgeoisie (French edition 1955; English 1957) remains a landmark critique, and his debate with Melville J. Herskovits over African cultural retentions structured a generation of scholarship. Howard's E. Franklin Frazier Research Center was inaugurated on May 24, 2000.

name: Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History
aliases: The Wright Museum; International Afro-American Museum
description: The Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History in Detroit was founded in 1965 by Dr. Charles H. Wright, an obstetrician, together with thirty other founders, as the International Afro-American Museum; it opened in January 1966 at 1549 West Grand Boulevard. The museum's current home, a 125,000-square-foot facility at 315 East Warren Avenue, opened in 1997. Its collection holds more than 35,000 artifacts, and its core exhibition, And Still We Rise, spans 22,000 square feet. The museum houses the National Museum of the Tuskegee Airmen and produces the annual African World Festival. Its rotunda has served the nation's mourning: Rosa Parks lay in state there in 2005 and Aretha Franklin in 2018. The Wright is one of the largest African American history museums in the United States and the institutional anchor of Detroit's cultural center.

name: Cab Calloway
description: Cab Calloway (Cabell Calloway III, born December 25, 1907, Rochester, New York; died November 18, 1994, Hockessin, Delaware) was the singer, bandleader, and entertainer whose “hi-de-ho” scat made him the swing era's most theatrical frontman. Raised in Baltimore, he briefly attended law school in Chicago — Crane College — while singing in Chicago nightclubs, then reached New York in 1929 and sang “Ain't Misbehavin'” in Fats Waller's revue Connie's Hot Chocolates. From 1931 his orchestra was a house band at Harlem's Cotton Club alongside Duke Ellington's. “Minnie the Moocher,” first recorded in 1931, became the first record by a Black musician to sell one million copies, and his band employed Dizzy Gillespie, Ben Webster, Cozy Cole, and Milt Hinton. Calloway appeared in Stormy Weather (1943) and, at seventy-two, in The Blues Brothers (1980). He received the National Medal of Arts in 1993; “Minnie the Moocher” entered the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1999 and the National Recording Registry in 2019.

name: Fats Waller
description: Fats Waller (Thomas Wright Waller, born May 21, 1904, New York City; died December 15, 1943, near Kansas City, of pneumonia, aboard a train) was the stride pianist, organist, composer, and comic entertainer whose playing laid much of the basis for modern jazz piano. A student of James P. Johnson, he was a professional organist at fifteen and made his first recordings in October 1922 for Okeh. Waller copyrighted more than 400 songs, many written with lyricist Andy Razaf, including “Ain't Misbehavin'” (1929, written for the revue Connie's Hot Chocolates) and “Honeysuckle Rose.” From 1934 he recorded with his small band, Fats Waller and His Rhythm, and his wit at the keyboard made him a radio and film presence as well as a hitmaker. The 1978 Broadway revue Ain't Misbehavin' built a hit show from his catalog a generation after his death at thirty-nine.

name: Memphis Free Speech and Headlight
aliases: Memphis Free Speech; Free Speech and Headlight
description: The Memphis Free Speech and Headlight was the Memphis newspaper from which Ida B. Wells launched the anti-lynching crusade. It was founded in 1881 by the Reverend Taylor Nightingale at Beale Street Baptist Church as the Memphis Free Speech, and renamed the Memphis Free Speech and Headlight in 1888 when J. L. Fleming, formerly of the Marion Headlight, joined the paper. In 1889 Wells bought a one-third interest and became its editor, with Fleming as business manager and Nightingale as sales manager. After the March 1892 lynching of her friends Thomas Moss, Calvin McDowell, and Henry Stewart of the People's Grocery, Wells's editorial of May 21, 1892, told Black Memphians there was no justice for them in the courts and advised them to leave the city. On May 27, 1892, while Wells was in Philadelphia, a white mob destroyed the paper's office; death threats barred her return, and she continued the campaign from exile with Southern Horrors (1892). The state reference literature notes that no copy of the paper is known to survive.

name: Herman Roberts
description: Herman Roberts (born 1924, Beggs, Oklahoma; died February 1, 2021) moved to Chicago at twelve in the Great Migration, attended Burke Elementary and Englewood High School, and built one of Black Chicago's great hospitality empires from a taxicab fleet that reached thirty-five cabs. In the early 1950s he opened the Lucky Spot lounge, then the Roberts Show Lounge in his former cab garage, booking Nina Simone, Dinah Washington, Sarah Vaughan, Sammy Davis Jr., Sam Cooke, Redd Foxx, Moms Mabley, and Dick Gregory. His first Roberts Motel opened in 1960 on 63rd Street and grew to eight motels; the sixth, in 1970, was a 250-room complex, and the Roberts Motel 500 Room hosted the official kickoff of Harold Washington's mayoral campaign. The HistoryMakers calls him the nation's foremost African American hotel and motel owner. He also held an Oklahoma ranch where he struck oil in 1981. Congressman Danny K. Davis entered a tribute in the Congressional Record on March 18, 2021.

name: Quinta Brunson
description: Quinta Brunson (born December 21, 1989, Philadelphia) is the creator, executive producer, co-writer, and star of Abbott Elementary, ABC's mockumentary sitcom set in a Philadelphia public school, in which she plays second-grade teacher Janine Teagues. Brunson built her audience herself: her self-produced 2014 Instagram series, The Girl Who Has Never Been on a Nice Date, went viral, and she became a producer and performer at BuzzFeed Video before leaving to build her own work. She attended Temple University and left to pursue comedy. At the 74th Emmy Awards she became the first Black woman nominated three times in comedy categories in a single year and won Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series; at the 75th she became the first Black woman in more than forty years to win Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series. Abbott Elementary received a Peabody Award in 2022, and Brunson was named to the Time 100 that year.

name: Tha Carter III
description: Tha Carter III is the sixth studio album by Lil Wayne, released June 10, 2008, on Cash Money, Universal Motown, and Young Money. It debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 with 1,005,545 copies sold in its first week and reached 2.88 million copies by the end of 2008. Its singles — “Lollipop,” which held number one on the Hot 100 for five weeks, “A Milli,” “Got Money,” and “Mrs. Officer” — made Wayne the dominant popular musician of his moment; guests include Jay-Z, T-Pain, Kanye West, Babyface, and Robin Thicke, and “Lollipop” carries a credited posthumous appearance by Static Major, who died in February 2008. At the 2009 Grammy Awards the album was nominated for Album of the Year and won Best Rap Album, while “Lollipop” won Best Rap Song and “A Milli” won Best Rap Solo Performance. Rolling Stone placed the album on its 500 Greatest Albums list.

name: Mary Church Terrell
description: Mary Church Terrell (Mary Eliza Church Terrell, born September 23, 1863, Memphis; died July 24, 1954, Annapolis, aged 90) was a founder of the organized Black women's movement in America. The daughter of Robert Reed Church, who had been enslaved and became a Memphis millionaire, she earned bachelor's and master's degrees at Oberlin (master's 1888), among the first Black women in the country to hold college degrees, and taught at Washington's M Street School. In 1895 she became the first Black woman appointed to a major city's school board, serving Washington, D.C. She co-founded the National Association of Colored Women in 1896 and was its first president, founded the Colored Women's League of Washington in 1892, and was a charter member of the NAACP in 1909. In her late eighties she led the campaign that desegregated Washington's restaurants, won in District of Columbia v. Thompson (1953).

name: Motor Row District
description: The Motor Row District is Chicago's landmark automobile-row district along South Michigan Avenue between roughly 22nd and 25th Streets, with related buildings on Indiana and Wabash Avenues, on the Near South Side. Built out between 1905 and 1936, it is the largest intact early automobile row in the United States: at its peak, 116 makes of automobiles — Ford, Buick, Cadillac, Hudson, Studebaker, Packard, and dozens more — were sold from its showrooms. The district's Black cultural weight is equally specific: the Chicago Defender was headquartered on the Row, and Chess Records stood at 2120 South Michigan, itself a Chicago landmark since 1990. The Row declined from the Great Depression and the Second World War as the industry moved outward. The district was designated a Chicago Landmark on December 13, 2000, and listed on the National Register of Historic Places on November 18, 2002; recent redevelopment has recast it as a music and entertainment district.

name: S. A. Cosby
description: S. A. Cosby (Shawn Andre Cosby, born August 4, 1973, Newport News, Virginia) is the Southern noir novelist who has redrawn American crime fiction around Black working-class life in the rural South. A former funeral-home worker who lives in Gloucester, Virginia, Cosby published five crime novels in six years: My Darkest Prayer (2019); Blacktop Wasteland (2020), which won the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and an Anthony Award; Razorblade Tears (2021), an Edgar Award finalist, Anthony and International Thriller Writers award winner, and Dashiell Hammett Prize winner that landed on Barack Obama's summer reading list; All the Sinners Bleed (2023), named to more than forty best-of-year lists including Obama's; and King of Ashes (2025), whose screen rights drew the Obamas' Higher Ground and Steven Spielberg's interest. He has twice won the Anthony Award for short fiction and wrote the Marvel Crime novel Truth to Power, a Luke Cage story.

name: Walter Mosley
description: Walter Mosley (born January 12, 1952, Los Angeles) is the novelist who brought the Black private-eye tradition into the literary mainstream with Ezekiel “Easy” Rawlins, the Watts factory worker turned reluctant detective. His debut, Devil in a Blue Dress (1990), set in 1948 Los Angeles, was named among the Mystery Writers of America's best hundred mystery novels and was filmed in 1995 with Denzel Washington as Rawlins. The Rawlins series has run for more than three decades alongside Mosley's Leonid McGill and Fearless Jones books, science fiction, plays, and essays. His publisher and the press describe him as the most important African American crime writer since Chester Himes, and he was a favorite author of President Bill Clinton. Mosley's work insists that the detective novel — America's most democratic form — belongs to Black Los Angeles as fully as to Chandler's.

name: Amandla Stenberg
description: Amandla Stenberg (born October 23, 1998, Los Angeles) is the actor who grew up in public at the center of young-adult Black storytelling. Her breakthrough came as Rue in The Hunger Games (2012), a performance that made a generation of young viewers attach to a Black girl character at the heart of a franchise. She headlined the romance Everything, Everything (2017) and won wide critical acclaim as Starr Carter in The Hate U Give (2018), adapted from Angie Thomas's novel about a police shooting's aftermath. She led the horror-comedy Bodies Bodies Bodies (2022) and played a dual role in the Star Wars series The Acolyte (2024). Stenberg is also a musician — half of the folk duo Honeywater, which debuted in 2015 — and was named to Time's list of most influential teenagers in both 2015 and 2016. Her name means “power” or “strength” in Zulu and Xhosa; her father is Danish and her mother African American.

name: National Bankers Association
aliases: Negro Bankers Association; National Negro Bankers Association
description: The National Bankers Association is the trade association of America's minority-owned banks, founded in 1927 as the Negro Bankers Association. Its organizing meeting brought nineteen Black banks together at Pythias Hall in Philadelphia in 1926, led by R. R. Wright of Philadelphia and C. C. Spaulding of Durham, North Carolina; the founding meeting followed in Durham in 1927. Renamed the National Bankers Association in 1948, it is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and describes itself as the voice of minority banking. Its membership — about one hundred institutions in the association's recent counts — spans twenty-two states and the District of Columbia, and has expanded beyond Black-owned banks to Hispanic-American, Asian-American, Native American, and women-owned institutions. For nearly a century the association has been the organized form of Black America's banking sector, the industry that financed much of the world this graph records.

name: Sidney Poitier
description: Sidney Poitier (born February 20, 1927, Miami, to Bahamian parents, and raised on Cat Island in the Bahamas; died January 6, 2022, Los Angeles, aged 94) was the actor who carried Black dignity into the American screen's center. Trained at the American Negro Theatre, he broke through in Blackboard Jungle (1955), earned the first Best Actor Oscar nomination given a Black man for The Defiant Ones (1958), and won the Academy Award for Best Actor for Lilies of the Field (the 1963 film; the award in 1964) — the first Black man, and first Bahamian, to win it. In 1967 he was the year's top box-office draw with To Sir, with Love, In the Heat of the Night, and Guess Who's Coming to Dinner. As a director he made Uptown Saturday Night (1974) and Stir Crazy (1980), then the highest-grossing film by a Black director. He received an Honorary Oscar in 2002, the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2009, and served as the Bahamas' ambassador to Japan from 1997 to 2007.

name: Mary McLeod Bethune
description: Mary McLeod Bethune (Mary Jane McLeod Bethune, born July 10, 1875, Mayesville, South Carolina, to parents who had been enslaved; died May 18, 1955, Daytona Beach, aged 79) built a college from $1.50 and a movement from that college. On October 3, 1904, she opened her Daytona school for Black girls with $1.50 in capital; through a 1923 merger it became Bethune-Cookman College, now Bethune-Cookman University. She presided over the National Association of Colored Women in 1924, founded the National Council of Negro Women in 1935 and served as its first president, advised President Franklin D. Roosevelt, organized the Federal Council on Negro Affairs — the “Black Cabinet” — and became the first Black woman to head a federal agency division, directing the National Youth Administration's Division of Negro Affairs. In 1945 she was the only Black woman holding an official role in the United States delegation at the founding conference of the United Nations. Ebony in July 1949 named her the “acknowledged First Lady of Negro America.”

name: Jesse Owens
description: Jesse Owens (James Cleveland Owens, born September 12, 1913, Oakville, Alabama; died March 31, 1980, Tucson, Arizona, of lung cancer, aged 66) was the track athlete whose four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics became the century's most famous athletic refutation of a racial doctrine. His family moved to Cleveland in 1922; at East Technical High School he tied the national 100-yard record of 9.4 seconds as a senior. At Ohio State — in an era without athletic scholarships, working part-time jobs — he produced sport's most famous afternoon: on May 25, 1935, at Ann Arbor, he set three world records and tied a fourth in about forty-five minutes, across the 100-yard dash, the long jump, the 220-yard dash, and the 220-yard low hurdles. In Berlin in August 1936 he won the 100 meters, the 200 meters, the long jump, and the 4×100-meter relay, the relay in a world-record 39.8 seconds. He came home to segregation and financial hardship. The nation honored him late: the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1976 and a posthumous Congressional Gold Medal in 1990.

name: Dorothy Height
description: Dorothy Height (Dorothy Irene Height, born March 24, 1912, Richmond, Virginia; died April 20, 2010, Washington, D.C., aged 98) was, in the phrase attached to her across the movement, its godmother. Raised in Rankin, Pennsylvania, she was admitted to Barnard College in 1929 and turned away under its quota for Black students; she took her bachelor's in education and her master's in psychology at New York University instead. On the Harlem YWCA staff she pushed the YWCA's national integration and founded its Center for Racial Justice. In 1937 she met Mary McLeod Bethune and joined the National Council of Negro Women, becoming its fourth president in 1957 and holding the post for forty years, until 1997. She helped organize the 1963 March on Washington — she sat on its platform, though the program gave her no speech — and ran the Wednesdays in Mississippi project joining Northern and Southern women. She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1994 and the Congressional Gold Medal in 2004.

name: Satchel Paige
description: Satchel Paige (Leroy Robert “Satchel” Paige, born July 7, 1906, Mobile, Alabama, per his birth certificate; died June 8, 1982, Kansas City) was the Negro leagues' greatest pitcher and its most famous showman, whose major-league chance came two decades late and still made history. He began in the Negro leagues in 1926–27 with the Chattanooga Black Lookouts, starred for the Birmingham Black Barons and the Kansas City Monarchs, and barnstormed the country — legend, in his own telling, sometimes sending his infielders to sit down while he struck out the side. On July 9, 1948, Cleveland signed him: at forty-two he became the oldest rookie in major-league history and the first Black pitcher in the American League, going 6–1 with a 2.48 earned run average and becoming the first Negro leagues player to pitch in a World Series, which Cleveland won. He was an All-Star with the St. Louis Browns in 1952 and 1953 and made his final major-league appearance on September 25, 1965, at fifty-nine, throwing three scoreless innings. In 1971 he became the first electee of the Hall of Fame's Negro League Committee inducted at Cooperstown.

name: Jayden Daniels
description: Jayden Daniels, born 18 December 2000 in Fontana, California, is an American professional football quarterback for the Washington Commanders. He began his college career at Arizona State, starting for three seasons, then transferred to LSU, where his second season, in 2023, became one of the most productive in college football history. At LSU he threw for 3,812 yards and 40 touchdowns against four interceptions and ran for 1,134 yards and ten more scores, leading the nation in total offense and winning the Heisman Trophy, the Davey O'Brien Award and AP Player of the Year. Washington drafted him second overall in 2024. As a rookie he set several rookie records, won NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, made the Pro Bowl and led Washington to its first NFC Championship Game appearance since the 1991 season. Injuries interrupted his 2025 campaign and the start of 2026, including a dislocated left elbow in Week 2, but he returned to start in October 2026, in his third NFL season.

name: Tyreek Hill
description: Tyreek Hill, born 1 March 1994 in Douglas, Georgia, is an American professional football wide receiver, nicknamed 'Cheetah' for his speed. Drafted by the Kansas City Chiefs in the fifth round in 2016, he made the Pro Bowl as a rookie returner and receiver and helped Kansas City win Super Bowl LIV after the 2019 season. In six seasons with the Chiefs he became one of the league's most feared deep threats. Traded to the Miami Dolphins in 2022, he produced consecutive 1,700-yard receiving seasons — 1,710 yards in 2022 and a franchise-record 1,799 yards with 13 touchdowns in 2023, when he led the NFL in receiving yards and was ranked first on the NFL Top 100. A dislocated left knee with multiple ligament tears in September 2025 ended his season after four games; Miami released him in February 2026, and in October 2026 he remained a free agent rehabilitating the knee while his agent discussed a return with multiple teams.

name: Ja'Marr Chase
description: Ja'Marr Chase, born Ja'Marr Anthony Chase on 1 March 2000 in Harvey, Louisiana, is an American professional football wide receiver for the Cincinnati Bengals. At LSU he was Joe Burrow's leading target on the 2019 national-championship team, winning the Fred Biletnikoff Award as the nation's top receiver that season before opting out of 2020. Cincinnati drafted him fifth overall in 2021, reuniting him with Burrow. He set the rookie single-game receiving record, won NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and reached Super Bowl LVI in his first season. After Pro Bowl seasons that established him among the league's elite, in 2024 he won the receiving triple crown — leading the NFL in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns — only the fifth player in the Super Bowl era to do so. He followed it with another First-team All-Pro season in 2025 and remained Cincinnati's No. 1 receiver in October 2026, scoring in the Bengals' Week 5 win at Miami.

name: Stefon Diggs
description: Stefon Diggs, born Stefon Marsean Diggs on 29 November 1993 in Gaithersburg, Maryland, is an American professional football wide receiver for the Washington Commanders. A Maryland Terrapin who stayed home for college, he was drafted by the Minnesota Vikings in the fifth round in 2015 and became a starter in Minnesota, where he caught the walk-off touchdown in the January 2018 playoff play known as the Minneapolis Miracle. Traded to Buffalo in 2020, he led the NFL in receptions and receiving yards that season, earned First-team All-Pro honors and made four straight Pro Bowls with the Bills. A 2024 trade sent him to Houston, where a torn ACL ended his season; he recovered to catch 85 passes for 1,013 yards for New England in 2025, reaching Super Bowl LX. Released by the Patriots in March 2026, he signed a one-year contract with Washington that August, a homecoming to the D.C. area, and was on the Commanders' roster — sidelined by a hamstring injury — in October 2026.

name: Jahmyr Gibbs
description: Jahmyr Gibbs, born 20 March 2002 in Dalton, Georgia, is an American professional football running back for the Detroit Lions. A dual-threat back at Georgia Tech, he transferred to Alabama for 2022, averaging 6.1 yards per carry and catching 44 passes in his single season with the Crimson Tide. Detroit selected him 12th overall in the 2023 NFL draft, a pick widely questioned at the time and quickly vindicated. Paired first with David Montgomery in Detroit's backfield, Gibbs made the Pro Bowl in each of his first three seasons. In 2024 he set a Detroit franchise record with 20 total touchdowns, leading the league, and scored four times in the Week 18 game that clinched the NFC's top seed. In October 2026 he was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week after a 207-yard scrimmage game at Arizona, in which he passed Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns scored before age 25 in NFL history.

name: Antonio Brown
description: Antonio Brown, born Antonio Tavaris Brown Sr. on 10 July 1988 in Miami, Florida, is a retired American professional football wide receiver. Raised in Miami's Liberty City and a walk-on turned All-American punt returner at Central Michigan, he was drafted by the Pittsburgh Steelers in the sixth round in 2010. In Pittsburgh he became the league's most productive receiver of the 2010s: seven Pro Bowls, four straight First-team All-Pro selections, league leads in receptions and receiving yards, and more receptions than any other player across 2010–2018. His Steelers tenure ended in a trade in 2019; he never played a regular-season game for Oakland, played one game for New England, then joined Tampa Bay, catching a touchdown in Super Bowl LV. His career effectively ended in January 2022, when he left the field mid-game for Tampa Bay and was released. Off-field legal matters, addressed in one neutral line in the notes, have continued after his playing career.

name: Cam Newton
