Under Kutza the festival championed early work by Martin Scorsese (whose first feature it premiered in 1967), Rainer Werner Fassbinder, Wim Wenders, Claude Lelouch, Mike Leigh and Michael Moore, and hosted guests from Harold Lloyd and Bette Davis to Spike Lee, Halle Berry and Chadwick Boseman. He is the author of the memoir Starstruck: How I Magically Transformed Chicago into Hollywood for More Than Fifty Years, remains CEO Emeritus of Cinema/Chicago, and personally selects the festival's Founder's Award.

name: Black Perspectives
description: Black Perspectives is the Chicago International Film Festival's program devoted to Black American cinema and films of the African diaspora, founded in 1997 in collaboration with Spike Lee and presented by Cinema/Chicago. The festival states the program's purpose as highlighting the excellence and diversity of Black American cinema and diaspora filmmaking; across three decades it has premiered Ava DuVernay's first feature and presented work by Barry Jenkins, Maya Angelou, Djibril Diop Mambéty, Abderrahmane Sissako and Steve McQueen, and the festival has honored Viola Davis, Forest Whitaker, Sidney Poitier, Halle Berry, Morgan Freeman and Pam Grier in the program's history. The program now runs year-round. Its 30th anniversary anchored the 62nd festival in October 2026: a Career Achievement Award evening for Marlon Wayans at the Logan Center on October 19, moderated by Omar Epps; Cheryl Dunye's Career Achievement tribute with a retrospective screening of The Watermelon Woman; Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor's Tour de Force Award at the world premiere of Liz Here Now; Sophie Okonedo's Spotlight Award at the Centerpiece presentation of Mouse; new work by Ava DuVernay (14th) and David Greaves (Once Upon a Time in Harlem); a twelve-feature slate spanning the United States, France, Senegal, Rwanda, Haiti and Brazil; and a seven-film shorts program, Love With No Place to Go.

name: WVON 40 Under 40 Game Changers
aliases: 40 Under 40 Game Changers; WVON Game Changers; COMPASS: The Navigators of Next
description: WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers is the Chicago Black talk station's honor program recognizing dynamic leaders under 40 who are making meaningful impact across Chicago and beyond — in business, innovation, community, culture, media, health, education and civic leadership. Eligibility, per the program: nominees must be 39 years old or younger by the eligibility deadline and demonstrate Chicago impact, leadership, innovation or service, and community influence. The program is sponsored by BMO. Its 2026 edition runs under the theme 'COMPASS: The Navigators of Next'; the Class of 2026 as published names 43 honorees — three more than the '40' brand, a discrepancy this record states rather than smooths — and the class is celebrated on Thursday, October 29, 2026, with a keynote by Dr. Louis Carr, President of BET. The program site publishes no celebration venue.

name: Aaron Mallory
description: Aaron Mallory is the founder and CEO of GRO Community, a Chicago-based nonprofit delivering culturally grounded, trauma-informed mental health and social services for boys and men of color, including therapy, workforce supports and reentry services. A licensed clinical social worker in Illinois, he holds an MSW from the University of Chicago and previously held direct-service and leadership roles at UCAN and Heartland Alliance, where he was Clinical Director of the READI initiative; his professional biography credits him with more than ten years in the field. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Aaron Smoot
description: Aaron Smoot is Community Engagement & Advancement Manager at The CAFE Group (the Cleveland Avenue Foundation for Education), a Chicago-founded national nonprofit established in 2014 by Don and Liz Thompson that supports students and education leaders of color; its 1954 Project awards $1 million grants to Black-led education nonprofits. Smoot was named a Surge Fellowship Chicago 2027 Fellow under that title. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Alexa Rice
description: Alexa Rice is the founder of Beech Beauty, a Chicago beauty company launched with a line of high-shine lip glosses, a portion of whose proceeds funds tree planting in underserved urban communities. Coverage in JWC Media and AfroTech (reporting WBEZ Chicago) identifies her as a granddaughter of John H. and Eunice Johnson, founders of Johnson Publishing Company (Ebony and Jet) and Fashion Fair, and reports that she developed the brand during the final year of her master's program at Harvard Divinity School. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Allen C. Shelton
description: Allen C. Shelton is co-founder and Chief Creative Officer of Narratent Digital Marketing, a Chicago digital marketing and branding agency whose partnerships have included NBC Sports, BET Media Group and Universal Music Group; he leads the agency alongside CEO and co-founder Desmon Walker, a fellow Southern Illinois University graduate. WVON's roster credits him in the shortened form 'Founder & CCO.' He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Ariel D. Rainey
description: Ariel D. Rainey — spelled Ariel DeNey Rainey in Obama Foundation and organizational sources — is the founder and CEO of Hustle Mommies, a Chicago nonprofit that equips urban and Black mothers to lead in business, policy and community through trauma-informed advocacy, economic empowerment and entrepreneurship. The Obama Foundation named her a 2025–2026 USA Leader, crediting her with mobilizing more than 3,500 mothers, helping secure over $125,000 in startup funding for Black mom-owned businesses, and founding the 'Paint the Hood Orange' gun-violence initiative. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Aris Singleton
description: Aris Singleton is CEO of Thank God It's Natural (tgin), the Black-owned textured hair and skincare brand founded in 2009 by her aunt, Chris-Tia Donaldson, and sold at Target, Walmart, Ulta Beauty, Sally Beauty, Walgreens and CVS. Singleton, who holds a BA in Finance from Texas Southern University, returned to the company in 2017 and became CEO following Donaldson's death in November 2021. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Ashlee Feemster
description: Ashlee Feemster is a Director at BET (Black Entertainment Television) in Chicago, credited on WVON's Class of 2026 roster as Director, Brand Solutions. The Chicago Advertising Federation's membership directory lists her as Director, Integrated Marketing at BET, and professional-profile data places her in BET's Brand Solutions function in the Greater Chicago Area at manager level before the rostered directorship; the roster's exact title wording is not independently confirmed. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Ashley Coleman
description: Ashley Coleman is President of C&G Construction Supply Company, a Calumet City, Illinois construction-supply firm the company describes as 100% minority- and women-owned, certified at city, county, state and national levels and founded in 2009. Her presidency is documented on WVON's Class of 2026 roster; no independent source naming her was located in this pass. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Brittany Winstead
description: Brittany Winstead, PharmD, RPh, is Associate Director, Program Management — Solid Tumor at AbbVie, the biopharmaceutical company headquartered in North Chicago, Illinois; AbbVie's own site identifies her in that role and as Global Chair of its Black Business Network employee resource group. WVON's roster renders her title in the form 'Associate Director, R&D Oncology' (solid tumor being AbbVie's oncology program area). She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Chardai Johnson
description: Chardai Johnson is Managing Director and Head of the Economic Equity Advisory Group at BMO Bank N.A., the bank practice that cultivates relationships with Black-owned businesses to expand access to capital; HOPE Chicago's leadership page confirms the title verbatim. At BMO since 2012, she previously led a U.S. Commercial Banking team serving family-owned and private businesses, was named a Rising Star Women Leader of Banking for 2024, and has held trustee and board roles with the ChiArts Foundation and Horizons for Youth. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Cleopatra Draper
description: Cleopatra Draper is a radio personality at WVON 1690 AM, Chicago's Black talk station, where she has worked in various capacities since 2019 and in January 2025 took the weekday midday slot (9 a.m.–12 noon), succeeding retired host Perri Small. She holds a master's in social work from the University of Illinois Chicago and founded Roses in Roseland, a nonprofit distributing household goods and groceries. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Corey Williams
description: Corey Williams — the Chicago West Side designer Corey Demon Williams — is the designer, stylist, children's author and actor behind GRÉVYI, a Chicago fashion brand presenting streetwear-meets-couture runway collections, including the sold-out Chicago Fashion Week show 'If You Haven't Been to Paris' on the West Side in October 2025; a public biography styles him CEO and Creative Director of GRÉVYI Clothing. He is not the former NBA player of the same name. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Corinth Jackson
description: Corinth Jackson is Chief of Staff for Obama Presidential Center Operations at the Obama Foundation, where — in her own statement as a Bisnow Chicago Women Leading Real Estate honoree — she leads strategic and operational planning for the Obama Presidential Center, the museum and civic campus in Jackson Park on Chicago's South Side planned to open in June 2026. World Business Chicago listed her in an earlier Center role, Senior Operations Associate, in 2024. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Destiny Singleton
description: Destiny Singleton serves as the 2025–2026 Honorary Student Board Member of the Chicago Board of Education, the student seat that represents the interests and perspectives of all Chicago Public Schools students at Board meetings; the Board's official agenda of action records her term as June 26, 2025 to June 25, 2026. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026. This record carries honor and role facts only.

name: Dixon Romeo
description: Dixon Romeo is the inaugural Executive Director of Southside Together, the South Side Chicago community-organizing organization formed by the merger of STOP and Not Me We — the latter of which he co-founded and previously led as Executive Director. The organization continues that work on housing, health, youth, education and mutual aid across Woodlawn, South Shore, Greater Grand Crossing and Park Manor, including tenant-union organizing, and 2025 coverage still cites him in the role. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Karen Fields-Lever
description: Dr. Karen Fields-Lever is the owner and founder of 28 to Brush Dental Studio (28 to BRUSH), the Forest Park, Illinois dental practice she opened in 2014, providing general and cosmetic care together with a mobile dentistry program — launched in 2016 and reported to have served more than 16,000 students — in schools and community centers. A Spelman College and Howard University College of Dentistry graduate, she completed a residency at Yale. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Iisha Scott
description: Iisha Scott is a meteorologist with NBC Chicago (WMAQ, NBC 5), credited in the station's own coverage as an NBC 5 Storm Team meteorologist. An award-winning Certified Broadcast Meteorologist holding the AMS seal, she earned a BS in Mass Communications from Norfolk State University and a BS in Geosciences/Broadcast Meteorology from Mississippi State University, and joined NBC Chicago in August 2021 from WCNC Charlotte, where she was a weekend meteorologist. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Jamila Trimuel
description: Jamila Trimuel is the founder and CEO of Ladies of Virtue (LOV), the Chicago nonprofit she founded in 2011 that prepares Black girls ages 9–24 to become confident, purpose-driven leaders through mentorship, leadership training and community service, serving more than 2,000 girls and women annually. Her recognitions include Obama Administration Change Agent honors with an invitation to the 2016 White House United State of Women Summit, selection as a 2023 PepsiCo Changemaker, and TEDx speaking. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Janella Curtis
description: Janella Curtis is the founder and CEO of Notary Nook, her Chicago notary and loan-signing practice — she is an Illinois-commissioned notary public, a remote online notary and a certified loan signing agent with 250+ completed signings on her professional profile — and the creator of NookScan Protocol, a patent-pending, AI-powered document-compliance platform she describes as designed to catch errors before execution; in a published statement she dates founding both in August 2025. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Jessica Barnes
description: Jessica Barnes is Senior Counsel at Gordon Rees Scully Mansukhani (GRSM), the national Am Law 100 law firm founded in 1974 and described as the first and only firm with offices in all 50 states. Her role is documented on WVON's Class of 2026 roster; no firm biography or other independent source for this Jessica Barnes was located in this pass, and other attorneys of the same name (including in Pittsburgh and Orange County) were excluded as namesakes. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Joy Joshua
description: Joy Joshua is the founder of Journey & Thingz, the Chicago mobile arts business she launched in 2022 offering jewelry-making, art and STEM workshops for schools, community programming, private events and corporate team-building; WVON's roster credits her as Founder & Creative Director. She also works as a Food Education Program Assistant for the 61st Street Farmers Market at Experimental Station, the Woodlawn nonprofit whose profile of the market recounts her business's launch. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Kalia Coleman
description: Kalia Coleman is a Partner at Riley Safer Holmes & Cancila LLP (RSHC), the Chicago-headquartered national litigation firm founded in 2016, practicing in government enforcement, investigations and white-collar criminal defense. She joined RSHC after nearly six years as an Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, most recently as Deputy Chief of the General Crimes Division, and previously served as an Assistant State's Attorney in the Cook County State's Attorney's Office. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Kenneth Griffin
description: Kenneth Griffin is the founder of No Matter What, a Chicago 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in Englewood in 2015 that invests in Chicagoland youth through mentorship, career readiness, mental-health healing, a community garden, culinary camp and summer travel. DePaul University identifies him as a DePaul graduate (SCPS '25, in nonprofit management), a Chicago police officer and chef who received the American Red Cross of Greater Chicago's Law Enforcement Hero award. He is not Kenneth C. Griffin, the Citadel founder and investor. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Kiearrah Lawrence
description: Kiearrah Lawrence is an AbbVie marketing leader credited on WVON's roster as Associate Director, Marketing; the Healthcare Businesswomen's Association named her a 2026 Rising Star for AbbVie Inc. Indiana University's 2022 coverage of the Kelley Direct Online MBA placed her in AbbVie finance and accounting while leading the company's African American employee resource group, the Black Business Network — the marketing directorship the roster records is her current role. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Krista Whitaker
description: Krista Whitaker is Executive Vice President of Legal and Business Affairs and Chief Legal Officer of the Chicago Bears, appointed April 9, 2024; the club states she leads its legal and security departments and works closely with President & CEO Kevin Warren across football and business operations. She joined the Bears from the Miami Heat, where she rose from Senior Associate Counsel (2021) to Vice President & Associate General Counsel, after roughly five years as a sports-law corporate associate at Proskauer Rose; she earned her JD at Stanford Law School in 2015 and was honored in 2025 by the Black Women Lawyers' Association of Greater Chicago. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Kyle Gardner
description: Kyle Gardner is CEO and Co-Founder of Dobson Avenue Capital Partners, LLC, a private investment firm supporting underrepresented entrepreneurs — the title given by Autism Speaks, where he chairs the Upper Midwest leadership council, and by the 2020 launch of The Empower Project for Black-owned consumer-goods businesses, in which Dobson Avenue provided advisory guidance and monetary investment. WVON's roster credits him in the lighter form 'Angel Investor.' He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Lauren Green
description: Lauren Green is Vice President of C&G Construction Supply Company, the Calumet City, Illinois construction-material supplier the company describes as 100% minority- and women-owned, established in 2009 and certified MBE/WBE at national, state, county and City of Chicago levels. Her vice presidency is documented on WVON's Class of 2026 roster; no independent source naming her was located in this pass, and other Chicago professionals of the same name were excluded as namesakes. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Leah Fulton
description: Leah Fulton is Vice President of Programs at Chicago Scholars, the foundation that selects, trains and mentors academically ambitious students from under-resourced Chicago communities through college completion and into civic leadership; announced on July 22, 2025 after a nationwide search, she oversees its college-access and college-success programming. She holds a PhD in Higher Education from the University of Minnesota, brings sixteen years in higher-education leadership, and previously served as Vice President for Student Life at Trinity Christian College in Palos Heights. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Makunde Martin
description: Makunde Martin is a co-founder of Chi Tech Collective, the Chicago community designed by and for Black technologists that addresses South Side disinvestment through education, mentorship, networking and pathways to tech employment and funding; 1871 also describes him as a software engineer at Google and a Campus 1871 speaker. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Malik Jackson
description: Malik Jackson is the publisher of the Chicago Reader, the nationally recognized alternative weekly founded in 1971 and known for community-centered journalism, investigative reporting and extensive local arts coverage; he took the role on June 1 under owner Noisy Creek, after serving as executive director and publisher of South Side Media Works, which operates South Side Weekly and the Hyde Park Herald. A third-generation Chicagoan who studied urban planning, he is not the NFL defensive lineman of the same name. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Malik Zambezi
description: Malik Zambezi is a Chicago-based documentary and street photographer working as 'Malik Shot You,' photographing people and places in Chicago communities not often represented. The Citizen Newspaper Group profiled his photography art walks through Chicago neighborhoods, the first running in Bronzeville from Metcalfe Park to Shawn Michelle's on 47th Street in October 2025. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Moriah Dowd
description: Moriah Dowd is a digital producer credited to Mean Media on WVON's Class of 2026 roster. No publicly identifiable organization matching that credit, and no independent source confirming her role, could be located in this pass; an older item naming a Moriah Dowd as a student filmmaker could not be confirmed as the same person and is not relied on. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Nina Idemudia
description: Nina Idemudia, AICP, is Chief Executive Officer of the Center for Neighborhood Technology (CNT), the Chicago urban-innovation organization founded in 1978; she joined as CEO in September 2023 after serving as Chicago Recovery Plan Director in the Chicago Department of Planning and Development, Director of Planning at MUSE Community + Design, and a planner for the City of Los Angeles. Crain's Chicago Business named her to its own 40 Under 40 in 2024, and she was elected the first Black president of the Illinois chapter of the American Planning Association in 2021. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Oscar Joyo
description: Oscar Joyo is a Malawian-born, Chicago-based visual artist — painter, illustrator, digital artist and muralist — whose work mixes Afrofuturism and Afrosurrealism. The University of Illinois Center for Advanced Study hosted him as a GAM Visiting Artist, with a lecture on February 26, 2026, and he created a mural for the Champaign County African American Heritage Trail; his work has been shown at Chicago galleries including Vertical Gallery. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Rahim Thompson
description: Rahim Thompson is Senior Program Manager at the Illinois Holocaust Museum & Education Center in Skokie, Illinois, where he has developed more than 200 public programs spanning antisemitism, genocide, LGBTQ+ rights and racial justice. The Association of Midwest Museums named him a 2025 Promising Leadership Award honoree; PMI lists him among its Future 50 honorees, and IPMA named him its Young Project Manager of the Year 2025 (Gold). His background spans project management, journalism and production. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Ciera Bates-Chamberlain
description: The Rev. Ciera Bates-Chamberlain is the founder and Executive Director of Live Free Illinois, which mobilizes Black churches and faith communities across Illinois to end gun violence and mass incarceration and to build safe, economically viable, self-sustained Black communities. The Obama Foundation named her a 2024–2025 USA Leader, crediting her with convening statewide clergy and nonprofit coalitions and developing violence-reduction and gun-violence and incarceration-reform programs. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Ronnie Mosley
description: Ronnie Mosley is the Alderman of Chicago's 21st Ward on the Far South Side — a ward spanning parts of Washington Heights, West Pullman, Morgan Park, Auburn Gresham, Beverly, Chatham and Roseland — sworn in on May 15, 2023 after winning the 2023 runoff election with 52% and succeeding Howard Brookins; at his election he was the City Council's youngest member. Before office he co-founded the policy and organizing firm Homegrown Strategy Group (2017) and worked in Alderman Michelle A. Harris's office (2015–2017). He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Shantel Franklin
description: Shantel Franklin is the Democratic nominee for Illinois State Representative in House District 8 in the November 2026 general election, running unopposed for the seat being vacated by Rep. La Shawn Ford; the district covers parts of Chicago's Austin neighborhood plus Oak Park, Forest Park, Brookfield and North Riverside. Southern Illinois University describes her as the first woman and youngest Democratic nominee for the district. A Southern Illinois University Carbondale political science graduate (2016) and former Alexander Lane intern in the Illinois Senate President's Office, she served six years in the Illinois Attorney General's Office in community outreach and as a legislative liaison, per her campaign. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Stevie Valles
description: Stevie Valles leads Chicago Votes, the nonpartisan nonprofit that empowers young Black and brown Chicagoans with political knowledge, leadership development and voter turnout, including voting access for incarcerated people. His title varies by source: 2026 releases, including a PR Newswire get-out-the-vote coalition announcement naming him a leader of the Reimagine Civics Coalition, title him Executive Director, while WVON's roster and an October 2026 event listing style him CEO; this record carries the roster's styling with the variance stated. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Teryn Payne
description: Teryn Payne is a journalist-turned-public-relations specialist on Chance the Rapper's executive team at CTR (Chance the Rapper) LLC, per Vocalo/WBEZ, which recounts her bachelor's and master's degrees in journalism from the University of Illinois, a first job at EBONY Magazine as assistant to the editor-in-chief, later work as a Teen Vogue editor and freelance beauty writer for Allure, Glamour and Refinery29, and her 2019 return to Chicago; 2025 Chance the Rapper video credits list her under CTR Management. WVON's roster additionally credits her as CMO of The Retro Grill, the South Side Chicago restaurant; that title is roster-only in this pass. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Troy Vivrett
description: Troy Vivrett is co-founder and Chief Operating Officer of Southern Chicago, the modern, upscale Southern restaurant in Chicago's South Loop (2000 S. Wabash Ave.) serving contemporary Southern brunch, cocktails and dinner in a 6,700-square-foot space with a 140-seat patio and private event space. FSR Magazine describes the independent concept as created and owned by Vivrett and executive chef Xavier Vance. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Xavier Vance
description: Xavier Vance is the executive chef and co-founder of Southern Chicago, the South Loop restaurant he created with Troy Vivrett, aiming — in his words at opening — to reintroduce Chicagoans and visitors to Southern American cuisine with a fine-dining approach to classic Southern dishes. The restaurant's own team listing and trade coverage give his titles as Executive Chef and Co-Founder; the additional 'CEO' title appears on WVON's roster only and is carried as rostered. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.
